Luxonis launches OAK 4 FFC for five-camera robot vision

The RVC4 board offers 52 TOPS of aggregate AI compute and flexible camera placement, with development kits planned for November 2026.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗27 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Flexible camera placement

OAK 4 FFC supports up to five Luxonis camera modules around a six-core RVC4 processor with 52 TOPS of aggregate AI compute. Nine module options include 48 MP IMX586 color, 1 MP OV9282 and 5 MP OG05 global-shutter sensors. The compute rating is not an application-level AI benchmark.

Calibration and integration

Modules have factory intrinsic calibration; users arrange them and configure OAK Viewer. Inter-camera calibration uses overlapping views and ordinary textures. Linux-based Luxonis OS lets the board act as a main computer or perception coprocessor, with 2.5GbE, USB-C, CAN-FD and synchronization interfaces.

Pricing and delivery plans

The $849 development kit is scheduled for November 2026; the $729 barebone board for Q1 2027. Both prices already include a temporary $200 surcharge. Cameras are separate, starting at $34.99. The 36-gram barebone board requires developers to provide cooling, housing and power integration.
